summary: Treating compute as contribution can reward waste, amplify wealth-based influence, and transfer hidden review and environmental costs to a project.

points.text: A contributor can inflate tokens, samples, retries, or expensive-model calls without improving the artifact. Raw spend is unusually easy to game because the costly process is often invisible to maintainers.
Public recognition based on compute privileges well-funded actors and can become pay-to-influence even if no formal voting rights are granted.
Generated patches may be cheap for the sponsor but expensive for maintainers to understand, revise, and support; reporting inference cost without review cost externalizes the dominant burden.
Provider traces can expose prompts, proprietary code, pricing agreements, or user data, while closed model revisions and changing prices make apparently precise statements hard to reproduce.
